Let colors be \(0/1\). Fix a checkerboard \(B_{i,j}=i+j \pmod 2\), and write every board color as

\[
x_{i,j}=B_{i,j}\oplus p_{i,j}.
\]

Then a \(2\times2\) square is chesslike iff the four \(p\)-values in it are all equal.

Along any NW-SE or NE-SW diagonal, \(B\) is constant, so the original diagonal colors are constant exactly when the \(p\)-values are constant. Thus the diagonal condition becomes:

> no \(4\) consecutive equal \(p\)-values on any diagonal in either direction.

Now there are \(5\) NW-SE diagonals of length at least \(4\). Each must contain at least one adjacent pair with different \(p\)-values. That adjacent pair is the NW-SE diagonal of some \(2\times2\) block, making that block non-constant in \(p\), hence not chesslike. These \(5\) blocks are distinct, so at least \(5\) of the \(25\) \(2\times2\) blocks are not chesslike. Therefore the number of chesslike squares is at most

\[
25-5=20.
\]

This bound is attainable: take

\[
p_{i,j}=
\begin{cases}
0,& j\le 3,\\
1,& j\ge 4.
\end{cases}
\]

Then every diagonal of length at least \(4\) crosses the column \(3/4\) boundary, so no diagonal has \(4\) equal \(p\)-values. The only non-constant \(2\times2\) blocks in \(p\) are the \(5\) blocks crossing that boundary. Hence exactly \(20\) blocks are chesslike, and the corresponding coloring \(x_{i,j}=B_{i,j}\oplus p_{i,j}\) satisfies all conditions.

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
